title: Add Network Chart Mark

complexity.rationale: The force-directed layout itself is a native Vega `force` transform (run statically for ~300 iterations rather than live-animated, per requirements) — not custom physics. But this is the first mark in the codebase needing zoom/pan (no existing scale-range/signal infra to extend) and the first needing node dragging (mouse-event-to-position-signal binding, also with no precedent). Those two interaction primitives, plus click-to-pin neighbor isolation (a new adjacency computation from source/target pairs), are three separately-reasoned, non-precedented pieces landing in one mark — the definition of a 5, not a breadth issue.

summary: A source/target/label relationship mark laying out nodes via a statically-settled force simulation (Vega's `force` transform, ~300 iterations, not live-animated), supporting node drag, zoom/pan, and click-to-pin isolating a node's neighbors. First mark to introduce zoom/pan and drag interaction primitives to this codebase.
requirements: Accepts `source`, `target` (required, defining edges) and an optional `label` channel for node labeling
Lays out nodes via Vega's `force` transform run to a settled static state (fixed iteration count) rather than a continuously re-simulating live layout
Nodes are draggable — dragging repositions a node and its connected edges follow in real time
Supports zoom and pan over the node/edge canvas
Clicking a node pins it: isolates and highlights its direct neighbors (connected nodes/edges), dimming everything else, until clicked again or a background click clears the pin

edgeCases.case: A node with no edges (isolated node)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Renders at a force-settled position with no connected edges; not excluded from layout.
Renders as a self-loop or is filtered out — needs an explicit decision (see openQuestions) rather than silently breaking the force layout.
Each component settles independently under the force simulation; no requirement that they visually separate or overlap-avoid across components.

edgeCases.case: Dragging a node during/before force settling
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Drag is only enabled after the static force simulation has completed settling; dragging mid-simulation is out of scope since the layout isn't live-animated.

edgeCases.case: Panning/zooming while a node is pinned
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Pin state persists through pan/zoom — it's independent of viewport transform.

edgeCases.case: Clicking a node while another is already pinned
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Only one node can be pinned at a time; pinning a new node clears the previous pin, per the click-to-pin convention used elsewhere (Funnel, Sankey, Chord).
Node/edge colors resolve through the existing colorScheme-aware color scale.
S1-only for this spec; no S2 port until the mark stabilizes out of rc status.
Drag and zoom/pan are mouse-only in this initial version; keyboard-equivalent navigation is an explicit v1 gap, not silently omitted (see openQuestions).

crossCutting.notes: touchesControlledHighlight: click-to-pin neighbor isolation is a new adjacency-based highlight computation (not CONTROLLED_HIGHLIGHTED_TABLE/SERIES) but should reuse the same opacity-encode convention. touchesTooltipOrPopover: nodes/edges support ChartTooltip/ChartPopover, reusing existing interactive-mark plumbing. requiresNewSignalOrScale: true — this mark introduces the codebase's first zoom/pan signal pair (scale-range transform driven by wheel/drag-on-background events) and first per-node drag-position signal (mouse-event-bound x/y override on top of the force-settled position), plus a `pinnedNode` signal for click-to-pin. requiresS1S2Parity: false because this ships as a new s1-only rc-status mark, matching the Donut/BigNumber precedent; revisit once promoted out of rc.

implementationPlan.change: Create NetworkOptions/NetworkOptionsWithDefaults/NetworkSpecOptions with required `source`/`target` fields and an optional `label` field.
Export the new Network types.
Add NetworkOptions to the MarkOptions union.
Fully-populated defaultNetworkOptions fixture, including a self-referencing-edge variant and a disconnected-subgraph variant.

New shared module: addZoomPanSignals (wheel-zoom + drag-pan signal pair updating scale ranges), intended for reuse by add-chord-mark and add-geographic-mark — first implementation of this pattern in the codebase, so no existing file to extend.

addForceTransform (Vega `force` transform configured for a static/settled run, ~300 iterations, no live restart), addAdjacencyField (derives each node's neighbor-id set from source/target pairs, for click-to-pin lookups).
getNetworkNodeMark (draggable symbol — drag event bound to an x/y override signal per node), getNetworkEdgeMark (line/rule following connected node positions, including drag overrides).

addNetwork, addData (calls addForceTransform + addAdjacencyField), addSignals (pinnedNode, per-node drag-position signals, plus addZoomPanSignals + interactive-mark signals), setScales (color scale if used).
Unit tests for the shared zoom/pan signal helper.
Unit tests for addForceTransform and addAdjacencyField, including self-loop and disconnected-subgraph cases.
Unit tests for getNetworkNodeMark/getNetworkEdgeMark using the fixture.
Per-function tests for addData/addSignals/setScales.
Register networkCount: -1 in initializeComponentCounts, import addNetwork, add the 'network' switch case.
NetworkProps/NetworkElement, Omit-ing only fields replaced at the React boundary (ChartTooltip/ChartPopover children).
Render-null component holding prop defaults, placed under rc/ per the Donut/BigNumber rc-status precedent.
Barrel export.
Add `export * from './Network'`.
Import Network from '../rc' and add its displayName dispatch case.
Add Network to the sanitizeRscChartChildren import/list from '../rc'.
Update the toStrictEqual ChartOptions snapshot to include the new mark type at default values.
Basic story plus a DragAndPin interaction story.

openQuestions: How should self-referencing edges (source === target) render, if at all — a small self-loop arc, or filtered out entirely?

Is zoom/pan built as genuinely shared infrastructure up front (this spec's zoomPanUtils.ts), or should this spec proceed standalone and add-chord-mark/add-geographic-mark each get their own copy if scheduling means they land before this one is reconciled? Affects file ownership across the three specs.
What keyboard-accessible equivalent (if any) is planned for drag and zoom/pan in a follow-up, given mouse-only interaction is called out as a v1 gap?
